record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: Can multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, which evolve populations of candidate solutions to approximate trade-offs among several objectives, be designed around selection indicators other than hypervolume, such as inverted generational distance or Hausdorff-distance-style measures, so that selection remains computationally practical and still produces good Pareto-front approximations as the number of objectives increases?

evidence.quote: other performance measures as possible alternatives to the hypervolume.
other performance measures that could be used for selection but have not been explored

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-objective optimization problem in which one seeks to approximate the Pareto front of a vector-valued function f : X → R^m, where X is a decision space and m ≥ 2 is the number of objectives. A multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) maintains a finite population P ⊂ X of candidate solutions and iteratively applies variation operators (e.g., recombination and mutation) followed by an environmental selection step that chooses, from a parent–offspring pool, the population for the next generation.

Indicator-based MOEAs perform selection by optimizing a quality indicator I that maps any finite approximation set A ⊂ R^m to a real number measuring how well A approximates the Pareto front. The dominant choice in the literature is the hypervolume indicator, defined for a reference point r ∈ R^m as the Lebesgue measure of the set { y ∈ R^m : ∃ a ∈ A with a ≤ y ≤ r }. While theoretically attractive (Pareto-compliance), its exact computation is #P-hard in m, which limits scalability to many-objective problems (m ≥ 4).

Alternative indicators include:
 • Inverted Generational Distance (IGD): given a reference set Z ⊂ R^m approximating the true Pareto front, IGD(A) = (1/|Z|) Σ_{z ∈ Z} min_{a ∈ A} d(z, a), where d is the Euclidean distance.
 • Hausdorff-distance-based indicators (e.g., Δ_p), combining a generational-distance and an IGD term via an L_p averaging in order to obtain a metric on the space of finite sets.

Problem. Design environmental selection mechanisms for MOEAs based on quality indicators other than hypervolume (in particular IGD-type and Hausdorff-distance-type indicators) such that:
 (i) the selection step can be evaluated in time polynomial in the population size and in m;
 (ii) the resulting algorithms produce, on standard many-objective benchmark families, Pareto-front approximations whose quality (measured by Pareto-compliant indicators) remains competitive with, or improves upon, hypervolume-based selection as m grows;
 (iii) one can prove convergence or limit-distribution results characterizing the optimal finite approximation sets selected by the indicator (analogous to the known optimal μ-distributions for hypervolume).

Investigate which indicators admit such tractable, scalable, and theoretically grounded selection schemes.
artifact.status_search_result: Several indicator-based MOEAs using alternatives to hypervolume have been proposed, including IGD+-EMOA (Lopez & Coello), Δ_p-based algorithms, and an IGD-indicator-based algorithm for many-objective problems (8, 15, 20 objectives) using Utopian-Pareto-front reference points. Surveys (e.g., Falcón-Cardona & Coello, ACM Computing Surveys 2020) catalogue many such indicators and algorithms. Thus the general design question is partially addressed in practice, but a complete theoretical characterization (optimal distributions, convergence guarantees, fully scalable Pareto-compliant alternatives) remains open.

status_evidence.title: IGD Indicator-based Evolutionary Algorithm for Many-objective Optimization Problems
status_evidence.snippet: IGD indicator is employed in each generation to select the solutions with favorable convergence and diversity ... evaluated ... over optimization problems with 8-, 15-, and 20-objective.
status_evidence.claim: IGD-based selection has been implemented and tested at scale, showing alternatives to hypervolume are practical.

status_evidence.title: Indicator-based Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithms: A Comprehensive Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive survey of indicator-based MOEAs covering many alternatives to hypervolume.
status_evidence.claim: A substantial body of work exists using non-hypervolume indicators for selection.

status_evidence.title: IGD+-EMOA: A multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on IGD+
status_evidence.snippet: MOEA based on the weakly Pareto-compliant IGD+ indicator.
status_evidence.claim: Hausdorff/IGD-style Pareto-compliant variants have been designed for selection.
